newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 to 2.00 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 to 2.00 higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 to 2.00 cents per lb higher on Thursday, as traders expected the market to follow-through on Wednesday's gains.

New York arabica prices bounced back from recent losses of Wednesday, boosted by speculative short-covering. September contract rose 3.65 cents, to 161.50 cents, after ranging between 164.25 and 156.00 cents. Spot July, which expires on Monday, ended 2.75 cents higher, at 187.25 cents, while the outer months closed up 0.20 to 2.40 cents.
The July/September switch narrowed to 25.75 cents compared with 26.65 cents at the close on Tuesday, while the September/December switch widened to 13.00 cents from 11.95 cents.

Some traders filling chart gap on Wednesday between 159.50 and 161.00 cents basis September improved the market's technical outlook. They pegged September near-term resistance at 165.00-165.50 cents. On the downside, the 155.00 level was still seen as strong support.
CSCE reported after Wednesday's close that certified coffee inventories rose by 3,269 60-kg bags as of July 15, to 75,414 bags. An additional 39,229 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Thursday that there is no frost or freeze in sight this week in Brazil's coffee belt, with the lowest temperatures in major coffee-growing areas likely to range in the low 50s to the low 60s F (12-16 C) through Tuesday.

In other news, the Brazilian government sold about 92 percent, or 137,808 60-kg bags, of the 149,705 bags of coffee stocks offered to all segments of the coffee sector in its auction on Wednesday, according to Banco do Brasil.
London robusta futures were modestly higher early Thursday in light trading. At the midday break, benchmark September was up $10 at $1,630, after ranging from $1,635 to $1,620.
